# darkob

> darkob is a fast, stable async Python library for the Rubika and Shad
> messaging platforms. It provides a Bot API client (`Bot`), a userbot
> client (`Messenger`), and a Shad facade, plus routers, conversational
> state, keyboards for every documented button type, and the reliability
> primitives most bots hand-roll: retry policy, rate limiting, a circuit
> breaker, an offline send queue and resumable downloads.

Python 3.9–3.14 · MIT. Latest version: https://pypi.org/project/darkob/

## Hard rules for generated code

- Install with `pip install darkob`; import from `darkob`.
- Handlers are `async def handler(bot, event)` and are registered with
  decorators on a `Bot` instance.
- The second argument is `event`, never `message`. Use `event.chat_id`,
  `event.text`, `event.message_id`, `event.reply(...)`.
- Filters live in `darkob.bot.filters` and are **instantiated**:
  `IsGroup()`, not `IsGroup`. They compose with `&`, `|`, `~`.
- There is no `Dispatcher`, no `message_handler`, and no aiogram, Pyrogram
  or Telegram types. A `Bot` registers and dispatches.
- Do not invent methods. Anything not listed in the API section below does
  not exist on this version.
- Every public method exists in both sync and async form.

## Reliability primitives

- `Retry(attempts, backoff, jitter, max_delay)`: honoured by both surfaces; presets `Retry.none()`, `.aggressive()`, `.patient()`.
- `RateLimiter(rate, burst, per_chat_rate)`: token buckets, global and per chat, applied to every attempt including retries.
- `CircuitBreaker(threshold, reset_timeout)`: per endpoint; opens after consecutive failures, half-opens to probe.
- `SendQueue(bot, path=)`: `put()` sends or queues; transient failures only; `flush()`, `start()`, `stop()`.
- `ProtocolTracker(path=)`: snapshots the discovered endpoints, socket URL and app version, and reports drift.
- `Bot.download_file(..., resume=True)`: streams to disk and resumes by byte range.
